audit.why: 51.69% over 830 games. Levels 1-3 are a genuine skill check on who stuns first; from 4 the stun-Tibbers threshold beats anything Veigar can put together alone.

Veigar's spike is Phenomenal Evil stacking — permanent AP from spell hits, takedowns and Baleful Strike last hits — which pays off in teamfights rather than the lane rows. Primordial Burst is 120s at rank 1 and scales on missing health, making it a finisher, not an opener.
audit.corrected: Missing-health scaling added to breakdown.cooldowns and feeding; stack denial added to ahead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two texts credited Dark Matter with a stun.
audit.why: Dark Matter is damage only; Event Horizon is the sole source of CC in the kit, it stuns only on the edge of the cage, and it is 20/18.5/17/15.5/14s at 725 range. Telling an Annie to fear a Dark Matter stun makes her play the wrong ability and miss a 20-second free window when the cage whiffs.
audit.corrected: Corrected in wants.you[0], spikes[0].text, early and breakdown.cooldowns with the real cooldown.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Molten Shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 and only its EDGE stuns — stand near the centre or leave before it forms, and that 20 seconds is your whole green light. - Primordial Burst scales on your missing health, so never step up already chunked.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the cage: it is 20s at rank 1, so one whiff and stun-Tibbers ends him long before it returns.

edits.before: If Veigar gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Event Horizon (Cage) extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.
edits.after: If Veigar gets a kill his Phenomenal Evil stacks are permanent, so deny Baleful Strike its last hits by clearing the wave first, farm with Q refunds, and never step in chunked — Primordial Burst grows on missing health.

edits.before: Ahead, shrink the lane: hold the glow, zone Veigar off CS by existing, and Flash-Tibbers the recovery attempt — fed Annie ends games at 20.
edits.after: Ahead, hold the glow and deny Baleful Strike its last hits — each one is permanent AP. Flash-Tibbers his recovery step before the cage returns.

edits.before: Play around minion pushes carefully so you don't eat a surprise Dark Matter stun in the wave
edits.after: Watch the sky for Dark Matter, but it never stuns — only Event Horizon's edge does

edits.before: Whoever lands their stun first (your Q/passive-charge vs his Dark Matter/Event Horizon cage) usually wins the trade, so early levels come down to who mispositions first around minion waves.
edits.after: Whoever stuns first wins the trade — your passive-charged Q against a 20-second Event Horizon whose edge is the only part that stuns — so early levels come down to who mispositions around the wave.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are a coinflip poke war — both champions rely on a landed skillshot/stun to win the exchange, and Veigar's Dark Matter has a longer cooldown early that punishes him if he whiffs, but neither side has a big damage edge yet.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are a coinflip poke war — both sides rely on a landed stun to win the exchange, and Event Horizon is 20 seconds at rank 1, so a whiffed cage hands you a long free window, but neither side has a real damage edge yet.
